title: Client liveness policy + partial-handoff protocol for interrupted streaming with tool-call context
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem: When client connections drop mid-generation we need a safe, observable way to clean up partial outputs, preserve tool/function-call state where useful, and provide deterministic resume or graceful fallback behavior across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. This ticket designs and implements a client-liveness policy plus a "partial-handoff" protocol that encapsulates selection criteria for retention vs eviction, a minimal resume handshake, and a compatibility shim for older clients that don't support structured handoff tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Define liveness states (Active, GracePeriod, Quiesced, Evicted) and deterministic transitions based on heartbeat, windowed ACKs, and token TTL
Implement partial-handoff token: opaque, signed, model+prompt+kv-prefix-aware, and valid across compatible model variants
Server cleans up ephemeral KV cache and cached prefix slices for evicted sessions within configured GC windows
Clients that present partial-handoff token can resume generation with at-most-once semantics or trigger fallback short-circuit (reroll) based on policy
Compatibility shim: clients without token support receive explicit finalizer events and a short retention period before eviction
E2E test coverage for disconnect during tool call, disconnect mid-function-arg stream, and reconnect-resume with altered sequencing
implementation_notes: Plan: 1) Add heartbeat+ACK telemetry to streaming API (ws and http/2) and instrument server-side session state machine. 2) Create partial-handoff token service: signs metadata, TTL, and minimal KV pointers. Avoid including secret material. 3) On client disconnect, enter GracePeriod and emit finalizer event to audit log. If a tool call was in-flight, hold tool execution results until either client resumes or a configured failover rule triggers tool compensation (cancel/rollback) via worker. 4) Eviction path must trigger garbage-collection hooks to free KV cache and prefix caches. 5) Provide a lightweight compatibility path: older clients get a "session-closure" event and a server-side retain-for header; after expire server performs same GC but without resume token semantics.
decisions: Use a signed JWT-like token (HS256) for the partial-handoff token to avoid cross-service state storage; token encodes session_id, model_variant, prefix_hash, creation_ts, ttl
Retention TTL default: 60s for P0 latency workloads, configurable per-customer via Dedicated/Private policies
At-most-once resume semantics chosen to avoid duplicate tool invocations; tool caller will be responsible for idempotency keys and compensation mechanisms
Don't persist raw KV cache to durable store for resume; store only compact references (prefix hashes) to enable cache warm-up on resume and keep memory footprint bounded
timeline: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after ops incident where long-lived tool-call tasks leaked memory after client disconnect
2026-03-03: Spike completed — prototyped token format and server-side state machine (PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pulls/4132)
2026-03-05: Design review with PM and Security; security asked for token expiry and no secrets in token payload
2026-03-08: Implementation started — heartbeat + ack updated in streaming protocol; added metrics for grace-period events

2026-03-11: QA reproduced reconnect-resume scenario with tool-call in-flight; observed two failure modes: race between GC and worker completion, and client replay causing duplicated function-call side-effects
2026-03-12: Decided to require idempotency keys for tool calls and to implement a soft-lock on in-flight tool executions during grace period
risks_mitigation: Risk: Resume token replay across regions — mitigate by including region and epoch in token and verifying against server epoch before accept
Risk: Idempotency burden on customers — provide SDK helpers that generate and store idempotency keys for common tool call patterns
Risk: Increased memory for retained partial outputs — enforce adaptive retention limits and prefer compact prefix-hashes over full caches
tests: Unit: session-state transitions and token verification
Integration: simulated client disconnect mid-tool-call and resume with token under high-concurrency
E2E: compatibility test matrix for old clients (no token), new clients (token), and mixed-mode deployments
review_feedback: PM (Liam): prioritize clear observability for customer-impacting evictions
Security (Priya): ensure token revocation path for compromised keys; asked for key-rotation doc
Design (Ena): suggested adding a 'finalizer' structured output event that client SDKs can interpret to reconcile UI state

Add SDK helpers for idempotency and resume-token handling (DX team)
